claims.claim: Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the building of the Great Pyramid.
claims.where: spoken (hook, line 1); also post text: title
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, PMC9477388. pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov answered with a reCAPTCHA wall, so the identical full-text JATS XML was read from Europe PMC (ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9477388/fullTextXML), Significance, Introduction and chronology paragraph, reference list; Rosso 2021, 'Toxicology and snakes in Ptolemaic Egyptian dynasty: the suicide of Cleopatra', Toxicology Reports 8:676-695, doi:10.1016/j.toxrep.2021.03.004, PMC8042289, full-text XML from Europe PMC (peer-reviewed; NOT cited in SOURCES); NASA Image and Video Library records (images-api.nasa.gov, NASA agency data) AS11-40-5903, KSC-as11-40-5877
claims.note: A4: a viewer who swipes away at second two hears that Cleopatra's life sits nearer in time to 1969 than to the pyramid's construction. That is true on every chronology the paper lists. PNAS: 'the Great Pyramid of Giza (Khufu Pyramid)'; Khufu's accession 'ranges from 2613 to 2577 BCE (1σ) according to the 14C-based chronology ... 2589 BCE (2), 2554 BCE (41), or 2480 ± 5 BCE'. Khafre's accession is 'centered on ... 2448 ± 5 BCE' on the latest (Spence) dating, so the pyramid was built before c. 2450 BC even there. That is about 2,380 years before 69 BC, against 2,037 years from 69 BC to 1969. Rosso: 'Cleopatra VII was born at 69 BC'. NASA: 'Armstrong and Aldrin landed on the Moon July 20, 1969'. 'The building' (construction rather than completion) only makes the gap bigger. The title card shown with the hook (69-30 BC) is also true (see n7).

claims.claim: The pyramid was finished around twenty-five sixty BC.
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, PMC9477388. pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov answered with a reCAPTCHA wall, so the identical full-text JATS XML was read from Europe PMC (ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9477388/fullTextXML), Significance, Introduction and chronology paragraph, reference list; Erdil et al. 2025, PLOS ONE 20(5):e0314612, doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0314612, full text at journals.plos.org (Abstract, Introduction, Results, Conclusions)
claims.note: Confirmed as a derived round figure, not a quoted one. No source opened states a completion year, as SOURCES entry 1 says. PNAS places construction in Khufu's reign: 'The Khufu branch remained at a high-water level ... during the reigns of Khufu, Khafre, and Menkaure, facilitating the transportation of construction materials'. It gives Khafre's accession, which ends that window, as '2586 to 2548 BCE (1σ)' (14C) or 'centered on 2558 BCE' (Shaw), and it judges 'the use of the 14C chronology ... is preferable'. 'Around 2560' falls inside the 14C bracket and next to Shaw's date. PLOS ONE: 'the Low Chronology is no longer empirically supported for the Old and Middle Kingdoms', which backs the higher dating. 'Around' carries the spread. Weak point for a pedant: on Spence's astronomical dates (PNAS ref 42) completion would be c. 2450 BC.

The cited Roller passage could not be opened (see n37). Recommended: add Rosso 2021 to SOURCES, or have Roller re-checked from a network that can reach the preview. claims.claim: c. 2560 BC is 'the usual round figure for its completion, between the end of Khufu's reign and Khafre's accession on the radiocarbon and Shaw dates (Sheisha 2022)'; 'the lowest (Spence, 2480 BC) would make the pyramid about 80 years younger'
claims.source_checked: Sheisha et al. 2022, PNAS 119(37):e2202530119, doi:10.1073/pnas.2202530119, PMC9477388. pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov answered with a reCAPTCHA wall, so the identical full-text JATS XML was read from Europe PMC (ebi.ac.uk/europepmc/webservices/rest/PMC9477388/fullTextXML), Significance, Introduction and chronology paragraph, reference list
claims.note: Three problems. (a) Sheisha gives accession dates only, not the end of Khufu's reign, so it supports 'before Khafre's accession (2586-2548 BCE 14C; 2558 Shaw)' and no more. (b) 'The usual round figure' has no source. (c) '80 years younger' sets Spence's accession year (2480) against a completion date (2560). Like for like, Spence puts Khufu's accession 109 years after Shaw's (2480 vs 2589) and Khafre's 110 years after (2448 vs 2558), so completion would be c. 2450 BC, about 110 years younger. Change: reword as 'before Khafre's accession on the radiocarbon and Shaw dates', drop 'usual' or source it, and replace '80' with 'about 110'. The conclusion that the comparison holds is unaffected (n1).
